title: Block close: the first thousand years
hookLine: martyrs, monks, creeds, alphabets, and a church spread across continents

lines: SO GREAT A CLOUD OF WITNESSES.
cards: A stadium, packed, rows rising into the dark. Down on the track, one runner, tired, still going. That's roughly the picture the letter to the Hebrews paints.

After a long chapter naming the faithful of the past, Abel, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Moses, Rahab and more, it turns to the reader: "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses."
The stands are full. At the end of this block of the path, we look up at them.

teach.b: This block began with the apostles scattering: they went everywhere. Peter and Paul in Rome. The temple falling, the gospels written down before memories faded.

Then the martyrs: Ignatius on the road, calling himself God's wheat; Polycarp; Perpetua and Felicity, a noblewoman and an enslaved woman, sisters in the arena. Christians who stayed in the plague when others fled.
Then a turn: Constantine, a letter granting freedom for all, and the councils. Nicaea and its creed, true God from true God, and Athanasius standing against the world.

Then the monks and the builders of mercy: Antony in the desert, Pachomius' community, Basil's city for the sick, Macrina the teacher of teachers, Benedict asking monks to listen with the ear of the heart.
Then the long reach: Patrick and Brigid in Ireland, Columba on Iona, Hilda at Whitby, Caedmon finding his song in the stable, Bede finishing his work.

teach.h: FROM IONA TO KERALA TO CHINA.
teach.b: And east and south: Ethiopia, Armenia, the Thomas Christians of Kerala, monks with books arriving in China. Ephrem's women's choirs. A dome that seemed to hang from heaven.
Icons broken and carried home again. An oak felled, an alphabet made, envoys who couldn't tell heaven from earth. It isn't tidy.
There were quarrels, splits, emperors who used the church and Christians who used power badly, and the path has tried to say so.

teach.h: SO GREAT A CLOUD OF WITNESSES.
teach.b: But Hebrews' picture holds. In the letter's image, they're in the stands, and the race is still on. The verse goes on, in the King James words: "let us run with patience the race that is set before us."
Tomorrow a new block begins: the middle centuries, east and west, starting with a monastery where the prayer hardly stopped.

how: Christians remember the saints and martyrs of the early church in their calendars, names and churches; Catholic and Orthodox Christians keep their feast days, and some Protestant churches honor them as examples of faith.

o: the apostles who saw Jesus risen with their own eyes
people called to testify in court about a crime
the faithful who went before, pictured in the stands

s: the early church stayed around the Mediterranean
this block reached Ireland, Ethiopia, Armenia, Kerala and China.
Hebrews pictures the faithful of the past as a cloud of witnesses
and calls the reader to run the race with patience.
the path has told this block as a story with no quarrels
it has named splits, power misused, and icons broken.

games.q: you've reached the end of a long block of history: martyrs, councils, monks, missions. what do you do with it?
o: file it away. it's the past.
pick one person and carry them with you.
games.why: Hebrews pictures the faithful of the past as a crowd in the stands, and the race still on. today's practice: one name to carry.

practice: Let the names drift past, Perpetua, Antony, Macrina, Patrick, Bede, Ephrem, Thomas, Boniface, or one I haven't named, and pick the one who stuck, not the most important. Picture them in the stands, watching your race.
If you pray, thank God for them by name; if you don't, just thank them, quietly, across the centuries.

wordCard.voice: Witnesses. The cloud of the faithful dead the letter to the Hebrews pictures filling the stands: apostles, martyrs, monks, creeds, alphabets, a church spread across continents.

orig.note: Greek: cloud, the word in "so great a cloud of witnesses."

carryVoice: Your line: a great cloud. The stands are full, and the race goes on. Day eight hundred six, done.
